title: Neon Asteroids: 1v1 PvP Multiplayer Test (Opus 5.5 in 1/2 Day)  Mobile + Desktop
author: diablopabloIRL
selftext:
I've always had a hard time getting multiplayer networking to work when building from scratch, especially keeping it free or close to it. So I picked something simple, the classic Asteroids design, and made the whole thing about the multiplayer part: a 1v1 neon dogfight that runs in the browser on both phones and desktops, and lets them play against each other.

I built it with Claude (Opus 5.5) doing most of the coding. It's a single HTML file with:

* **Peer-to-peer connections (WebRTC)**, so there's no game server. Players find each other through free public relays, and there's a free backup relay for strict networks.
* **Hosting on GitHub Pages**, so the whole setup costs $0 right now.

I think I pulled it off, but would love people outside my friends and family to tell me if it actually works for them.

**How to play:** LAUNCH drops you into Quick Play and pairs you with a random person. You can also Host or Join a private match with a 4-letter code, or practice offline solo or against a bot. If nobody's in the queue, you can fight a bot while you wait, and it'll switch you into the real match the moment someone shows up.

**Play:** [https://deadbaron.com/neon-asteroids](https://deadbaron.com/neon-asteroids)

If you try it, I'd love to know:

* Did it connect, and roughly how long did it take?
* What device, browser and network (Wi-Fi, mobile data, work or school)?
* If it didn't connect, there's a Network Test button on the main menu. Copying that report here would help a ton.

I'll be on tonight from if anyone wants a match. Happy to answer questions about the setup, what worked, and what Claude struggled with.

comments.author: diablopabloIRL
